rationale_bullets: Washington's true-freshman baseline is real: 71.3 PFF/519 dropbacks (B10 +1 -> 72.3, at the p50 unit reference), 2,963 yds, 17-9, freshman school records, 773 yds in his first three games - best P4 true-FR debut since 2018 (P6).
Named context: he did it behind the FBS's worst run-blocking tape (RBLK 0th pctile) and a WR room leading the nation in drops - and the elite 2% sack rate was partly his quick release (P6).

The consensus trajectory is unusually strong and attributed: opposing B10 assistant - '[Washington] is elite... we hit him a couple times, and it just didn't bother him'; PS - spread refit means he 'should thrive... one of the top QBs in the Big Ten as a sophomore'; P6 - 'the usual second-year starter bonus.'
Growth areas cited, not hidden: 57% comp, #16 B10 QB rating (P6); new OC install (Trickett) is change on top of youth.
Depth is weak (Kargman: 51.6/19; 43% career at Kent State). 60, M = mechanical p51 plus the trajectory consensus, well short of proven-tape rooms like Indiana's Hoover (70).

rationale_bullets: Williams returns as the proven piece: 68.9 PFF/128 att (B10 -0), 501 rush @ 3.9 plus 426 receiving yds - most by a Maryland RB since 2001 (P6); 45 catches (Athlon).
Mechanical: 68.9 sits just below the p25 RB reference (Maryland '25 itself is the p25 aggregate at 69.6); the room's returning tape is bottom-quartile.
Additions are priors, not production: Dalton (USC rFr; 4* in the '25 class; 8 career att), Worthy (Temple), FR Coombs (PS#47); Ray (72.0/67) left for BC.

Context cuts both ways: 1,252 team rush yds (4.1) at #124 - but RBLK graded 0th percentile, so the line owns much of the output failure; PS: 'talent with everyone back' and a new OC hired to fix the ground game.
38, M = a tick over the Illinois-32 exemplar: comparable returning grades, better receiving value, similar line problem.
All three starting WRs depart (P6): Knotts (65.6/418; 717 @ 16.3), Farooq (64.6/377), O.Smith (55.3/460) - from a room that graded 7th percentile in RECV and led the nation in drops (Athlon).

The imports carry the room: Gladding 75.5/342 at Old Dominion (SBC -1 -> 74.5; All-Sun Belt) and Durr 67.9/222 at Wyoming (MWC -4 -> 63.9; their #1) - combined 96/1,136/10 in 2025 (P6, level-flagged).
Returners are unproven or low-graded: Webb (63.5/225; 22 rec @ 14.5), 4* Z.Smith (competing, per P6); TE Fleming caught 40 balls (2nd among B10 TEs) but graded 52.3/330 - volume without grade.

TE add Howard (Auburn) graded 40.0/197 - poor tape even with the SEC offset. [Erratum 2026-07-16: an earlier McDuffie clause removed - he is a Northwestern FR; contamination during page extraction. Grade unaffected.]
Weighted aggregate ~63 → ~p33. 40, M = bottom-third: one Sun-Belt-proven receiver, everything else projection - but a real floor-raise vs the 7th-pctile 2025 room.

rationale_bullets: The split-personality tape: PBLK 81st pctile with a 2% sack rate (#1 in P6's pass-pro metric, 9 sacks all year) vs RBLK 0th percentile and #128 Run Push - the worst run-blocking grade in FBS.

Three starters return (91 career starts - PS): Hershey 66.5/764 (All-B10-Academic C), Perry 55.3/752, and Wright 59.6/651 - the yr4 RETURNS override (Athlon two-deep bold + prose + PS unit math; P6's 'three starters gone' noted as the dissent, news.md).
GONE: the best tape - All-B10 Herron (71.2/760) - and Bah (60.7/681, to LSU).

IN: Lockette 72.0/277 at Texas State (SBC -0) - the best adjusted number on the projected line, 3-year starter; Gilchrist (Top100) back from a season-ending injury, 'should become an all-league star' (P6) but has no tape.

Weighted aggregate ~61 → ~p33 with the reliable-volume grades mediocre. 40, M = the experience mass and elite pass-pro skill hold it at bottom-third rather than bottom-quartile; the run game is the named fix mandate.

The edge pair is the case: Mathis 68.6/474 (B10 +10 -> 78.6; Top100, Shaun Alexander FR-of-Year semifinalist, 6 sk) + Stewart 63.3/585 (-> 73.3; FR All-American; school-record 10.5 TFL by a freshman) - 'already one of the best young pass rush duos in America' (P6) - plus five-star Zion Elee, the #1 DE and #5 overall recruit in the class (Athlon starts him at OLB day one).

The interior is the named problem: run D collapsed to 176 ypg (4.4) with six straight 190+ games (PS); RDEF 39th pctile; Fontus portaled (Syracuse) and yr4 Rice (71.4/566 - quietly the best full-volume tape) expired.

Interior answers are tape-thin: Thomas 64.2/397 (-> 74.2), 4* Jenkins 63.0/151 ('potential star' 350-lbr - P6), Taylor/Holmes rotation, LeBlanc 68.9/158 (UCF), Johnson (Texas - no volume, priors only), two Washington adds.
Mechanical: returning weighted aggregate ~75 (~p75) rides the B10 offset on year-one tape; the qualitative consensus (elite edges, soft middle) and the RDEF tape pull it down.
63, M = above-average: the edge talent is top-25-caliber, the interior is not, and Elee is unpriced upside.
